title: How AI is changing PhD programmes: join our free webinar
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 09 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02751-7

Learn how artificial intelligence can hone your research skills as well as the potential pitfalls of relying too heavily on it.
headline: AI tools are reshaping how PhD students learn research, but overreliance poses real risks.
why_it_matters: As artificial intelligence becomes more powerful, students and early-career researchers need to understand how to use it as a helper without letting it replace critical thinking. Learning to work *with* AI rather than *relying on* it will shape the next generation of scientists who solve medical problems, including cancer.
key_findings: AI can strengthen PhD training by automating routine tasks, freeing up time for students to focus on creative problem-solving and experimental design
Over-dependence on AI tools risks eroding core research skills like literature review, hypothesis development, and hands-on experimental thinking
Institutions need clear guidelines on when and how AI should be used in PhD programmes to maintain research quality and integrity
Students who understand both the capabilities and limitations of AI will be better equipped for careers in modern research
methods_snapshot: This is a perspective piece and webinar announcement rather than a formal research study. It synthesizes insights about AI's role in academic training and highlights both opportunities and cautionary lessons from early adoption of AI tools in PhD programmes.

glossary.definition: Computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human thinking, such as learning from examples and making decisions.
A multi-year university education leading to a doctorate degree, typically involving original research and training in specialized fields like biology or medicine.
Honesty and transparency in how scientists conduct, report, and share their work to ensure findings are trustworthy.

ml_angle: AI systems can help researchers rapidly analyze literature, design experiments, and process data—but students must still develop their own scientific intuition and judgment.
limitations: This commentary does not present experimental data or case studies; it is a call for thoughtful discussion rather than empirical evidence. The actual long-term effects of AI integration in PhD training remain unclear.
